paragraphs: A heavy bag hangs rather than stands, and that changes everything about how it reads. The filling settles toward the bottom so the bag is wider below than above, the top gathers into straps and a swivel, and the leather creases where it has been struck. A perfect cylinder looks like a column, not a bag.
The mesh is efficient at 23,239 polygons and 22,731 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the settled profile, the seams and the top strap assembly.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits gym and fitness visualisation, boxing and martial arts material, sports advertising, film and television training scenes, and games. On sale since 2025.

An intercontinental ballistic missile is defined by its size. This one is large enough that its transporter needs eleven axles, and the proportions show it: a very long two stage body, a wide diameter first stage and a blunt shroud at the nose covering the reentry vehicles. It is the scale that makes the weapon legible in a graphic.

The mesh is deliberately light at 8,917 polygons and 8,882 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is the right economy for an object whose interest is silhouette rather than surface detail.
At $49 it suits defence and geopolitical visualisation, news and documentary graphics, strategic analysis material, education content and games. On sale since 2022.

A control cabinet is a wall of interface: indicator lamps, selector switches, emergency stops, ammeters and a door that opens onto rows of breakers and terminal rails. The front is what a viewer reads, and every element on it is standardised in size and colour, which means the layout has to be plausible rather than decorative.
The mesh runs 77,402 polygons and 79,457 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the switch bodies, the lamp bezels and the door hardware.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits industrial and plant visualisation, electrical engineering presentation, factory and utility interiors, training and safety material, and games. On sale since 2024.

This is the same class of cabinet shown without contents, which suits equipment catalogues and specification material where the product rather than the application is the subject. Clean shelves, a closed glass door and the controller on the front are what a buyer compares between models.
The mesh is efficient at 58,739 polygons and 61,107 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the detail in the door seal, the shelf supports and the control panel.

At $49 it suits laboratory equipment marketing and catalogues, research and clinical visualisation, biotechnology and pharmaceutical presentation, science education material and games. On sale since 2021.

Lace is the difficulty here. It is a fabric defined by what is not there, so it has to be modelled as a surface with real transparency and a real pattern rather than as opaque cloth, and it has to sit against a form without intersecting it. Presented on a dummy, the garment holds its shape the way it does in a shop display.

The mesh is light at 6,653 polygons and 6,647 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a garment whose detail lives entirely in the texture and the alpha rather than in geometry.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits lingerie and apparel e-commerce, fashion retail visualisation, packaging and catalogue renders, store interior displays and games. On sale since 2025.

A hiking boot is built in layers that are all visible: a stiff sole with a deep lug pattern, a rand around the toe, a leather upper, a padded collar and a lacing system that changes from eyelets to hooks partway up. Each of those is a functional decision, and together they are what separates a boot from a shoe.
The mesh runs 105,606 polygons and 109,358 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the sole lugs, the stitching and the lace hardware.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits outdoor and adventure advertising, footwear retail and e-commerce renders, character set dressing for film, television and games, and equipment visualisation. On sale since 2024.

Consumer router design went somewhere strange in the last decade: angular faceted shells, swept wings and antenna arrays that look like they belong on a spacecraft. This one carries that language, and the faceting is exactly what makes it hard to fake with a texture - the shape has to be there.
The mesh is efficient at 22,650 polygons and 24,658 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the vent slots, the facet edges and the antenna wings.
At $49 it suits consumer electronics advertising, home and office interior visualisation, network and connectivity marketing, retail and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2021.

A neutron star is not a surface you can model. What can be shown is the environment around it: plasma streaming along field lines, hot spots at the magnetic poles and the twisting sheet where the field is dragged by rotation. That is a volumetric and animated problem rather than a geometric one.

This asset is prepared and animated for Blender, so the plasma behaviour and the timing are already solved in the renderer they were built for. Setting up that kind of volumetric motion from scratch is expensive in both machine time and expertise.

At $49 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits astronomy and science communication, planetarium and museum content, documentary and educational video, title sequences and motion graphics, and games. On sale since 2026.

A portrait bust of a living public figure is a demanding likeness problem: the face is familiar to millions from constant photography, so every proportion is checked instantly and unconsciously. Rendered as plaster rather than in colour, the sculpture is judged purely on form, with no texture or tone to help it.

The mesh is light at 10,236 polygons and 10,141 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is the right economy for a subject where the silhouette and the surface material carry everything.

At $49 and built to StemCell specification, it suits editorial and news illustration, political commentary and satire, exhibition and gallery visualisation, print and merchandise, and games. On sale since 2025.

This is a disposable launcher: a sealed fibreglass tube with the rocket already inside, end caps that pop off, a folding sight and a firing bar on top. After use the tube is discarded, which is why it has no reusable parts and why the whole thing weighs almost nothing compared with a reloadable launcher.
The mesh is efficient at 33,630 polygons and 17,078 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the sight, the firing mechanism and the end cap detail.

At $49 and built to StemCell specification, it suits defence and conflict visualisation, news and documentary graphics, film and television armouries, training material and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a character rig. On sale since 2023.

A suit jacket is judged at the lapel and the shoulder before anywhere else. The lapel has to roll rather than fold flat, the shoulder has to sit with the right amount of structure, and the front has to break correctly at the button. Those three areas are where tailoring is visible, and they are what a model has to get right.

The mesh is minimal at 5,000 polygons and 5,060 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 3 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the cloth weave, the stitching and the buttons.

At $49 it suits corporate and business visualisation, apparel retail and catalogue renders, character set dressing for film, television and games, and interior scenes needing figures. On sale since 2015.

A skateboard battery pack is the single most consequential shape in electric car design. It is a flat slab spanning the whole floor between the axles, which lowers the centre of gravity, frees the space an engine would use and dictates the proportions of every car built on it. Showing it separately is how that argument gets made.

The mesh is efficient at 24,337 polygons and 26,603 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the casing and the module detail.
At $49 it suits electric vehicle engineering and marketing, technical cutaways, battery and energy storage presentation, education and training material, and games. On sale since 2016.

A tiki bar is thatch, bamboo and rough timber assembled to look improvised while being anything but. The roof overhangs deeply, the counter is a single slab, the posts are irregular, and the whole structure sits directly on sand. That deliberate roughness is what has to be modelled, since anything too neat reads as a shopfitting.

The mesh is heavy for a small structure at 607,693 polygons and 855,065 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and the reason is the thatch: every frond is geometry, which is what makes the roof read correctly against a sky.
At $49 and built to StemCell specification, it suits resort and hospitality visualisation, beach and travel advertising, event and themed venue design, exterior renders and games. On sale since 2026.

An underwater rifle fires steel darts rather than bullets, because a conventional round is unstable in water. That single decision reshapes the weapon: the magazine is very deep to hold the long projectiles, the barrel is smoothbore, and the whole thing is built to work while flooded rather than to be kept dry.
The mesh runs 39,912 polygons and 40,701 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the corrosion resistant finish and the handling wear.

At $49 it suits combat diving and special operations visualisation, film and television armouries, games, documentary work and museum material. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a character rig. On sale since 2017.
